title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.12998v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Linear probes are a standard method to study geometric structures, such as helices and circles, from the activations of large language models (LLMs), and such structure is often taken as evidence that the model computes with it. Probe accuracy alone cannot establish this, because it conflates four separate claims. These are (1) that the concept is decodable from the activations, (2) that they form a specific shape, (3) that the shape belongs to the probed concept rather than to a related concept the model also represents, and (4) that the output of the model depends on the shape. We call these claims decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use, and we test them separately with a four-stage Bayesian pipeline. Stage 2 compares candidate shapes and selects the best one only when its evidence passes a predefined threshold. Stage 3 removes a set of related concepts, specified in advance, and tests whether the shape is owned or inherited.

translated_title: 从线性探针到贝叶斯流形：大语言模型中算术运算的几何结构
translated_abstract: 线性探针是从大语言模型（LLM）的激活值中研究几何结构（如螺旋线和圆）的标准方法，此类结构常被当作模型利用其进行计算的依据。然而，仅凭探针准确率无法证实这一点，因为它混淆了四个相互独立的命题：（1）概念可以从激活值中被解码；（2）这些概念构成特定形状；（3）该形状属于被探测的概念，而非模型同时表示的另一个相关概念；（4）模型的输出依赖于该形状。我们将这些命题分别称为可解码性、形状、归属权和因果使用，并通过一个四阶段的贝叶斯流程对它们分别进行检验。第二阶段比较候选形状，仅当其证据超过预定义阈值时才选出最佳形状。第三阶段移除一组预先指定的相关概念，检验该形状究竟是被探测概念所拥有，还是从相关概念继承而来。
tldr: 该论文提出一个四阶段贝叶斯分析流程，将探针准确率分解为可解码性、形状、归属权和因果使用四个独立命题并分别检验，从而更严谨地判定大语言模型激活中的几何结构（如编码算术运算的螺旋或圆形）是否真正被模型用于计算。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a four-stage Bayesian pipeline that decomposes probe accuracy into four separate claims—decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use—to rigorously determine whether geometric structures in LLM activations (such as helices and circles encoding arithmetic) are genuinely used by the model in its computations.
